biography: Michael Sauer, a Dane with ice in his veins and fire in his belly, didn't come from racing royalty. His father was a fisherman, and Michael spent his early years mending nets and battling the unpredictable North Sea. One stormy afternoon, sheltering in the harbor, he saw a battered kart being unloaded from a trailer. That was it. Hooked. He badgered his father relentlessly until the old man, seeing the spark in his son's eyes, relented and bought him the kart. Sauer clawed his way through the ranks, a raw talent tempered by the unforgiving conditions of amateur racing in Denmark. He built his name in national Formula Ford, impressing with late-braking overtakes and an uncanny ability to wring every last drop of performance from his machine. His debut season with Caterham Supersport was a revelation, instantly turning heads. Now, at 37, he's still pushing hard for wins.
drivingStyle: Sauer is an aggressive, late-braking specialist. He thrives on the edge, often flirting with the limits of grip in search of that extra tenth of a second. His corner entries are audacious, characterized by a 'dive-bomb' style that has earned him both admirers and detractors. He's known for his relentless pressure on opponents, forcing them into mistakes. While his tire management isn't his strongest suit, he compensates with raw speed and an unwavering commitment to attack.

rivalries.reason: Rossi, a calculating Italian, represents everything Sauer isn't. Their contrasting styles often lead to on-track clashes and heated exchanges in the paddock.
Mendoza, a young up-and-comer, publicly dismissed Sauer as 'past his prime.' Sauer is determined to prove him wrong.
Olsen and Sauer were teammates for a short period, but a controversial incident during a race, where Sauer aggressively overtook her, soured their relationship and created a bitter rivalry.

quirks: Always wears the same faded blue wristband his father gave him before every race.
Listens to a specific Danish folk song on repeat for an hour before getting in the car.
Sharpens all his pencils before a race, even if they don't need it.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula Ford Nordic Championship in 2012 after starting the final race from the back of the grid due to a mechanical failure in qualifying, showcasing his relentless determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2021 Caterham Supersport season finale, costing him the championship by a single point.
